title: Get a long board through a narrow doorway in a partition: turn it end-on, push it through and take it on the other side
instruction: Move the wooden board to the grey mat on the other side of the partition and lay it flat along the mat. It only fits through the narrow doorway end first.
context: Long items such as planks, pipes, curtain rods and ladders have to be carried through doorways and hatches much narrower than they are long: they are turned end-on, fed through, and taken by someone on the other side, then turned back. Between two work cells divided by a partition, two arms can only meet at the opening, so each has to do its half and hand over through it.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. A fixed light grey partition, 1.2 cm thick and 35 cm tall, runs straight out along the centre line from 8 to 52 cm forward and splits the table into a left and a right side; it has one doorway, 8 cm wide, from 26 to 34 cm forward. Neither arm reaches the far side of the partition. On the left side lies a pine board, 30 x 4 x 1.5 cm, 100 g, flat and parallel to the partition, its middle 30 cm forward and 20 cm left of the centre line. On the right side, a fixed grey mat, 34 x 8 cm and 1 mm thick, lies parallel to the partition, its middle 30 cm forward and 17 cm right of the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Measured from the overhead and wrist videos and with a ruler and a protractor. 1.0: the board lies flat on the mat, along it (its middle within 2 cm of the mat's middle, turned less than 10 degrees from the mat's long side), still for 2 s. 0.5: the whole board is on the right side of the partition but not lying on the mat as required. 0.0: anything else, including any part of the board still in the doorway or on the left side.
reset_notes: Lay the board back on its mark on the left side; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX (Isaac Sim 6.1, 20 Hz control) of a calibrated two-arm table. Simplified: the board is a rigid block, the partition and the mat fixed blocks. Loose objects get rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Dream-1 sees the 320 x 176 frames it expects; the demo video is rendered at 1280 x 720.
